Hi Maria — thanks for the note and the questionnaire. Looping in Ben (infra/ops) for the technical intake and Kim (legal) for redlines.

High-level proposal from our side:
- Intake & SLA: a two-step evidence intake: (1) a triage packet within 48 hours confirming what we have and what we need; (2) substantive evidence delivery within 5 business days for standard items, with defined escalation for sensitive/large data sets.
- Artifacts we can produce: request logs (anonymized where required), model binary artifact identifier (model hash + build id), inference metadata (timestamp, sequence length, token counts), and a sample of input/output where permitted. We cannot provide raw customer-submitted training data.
- Egress: we can provide secure S3 presigned uploads for large bundles.

Ben, can you add a short engineering note for Maria on what we can and cannot deliver and suggestions for how BrightLabs can package items to speed triage?

Kim, once we have Ben's note I suggest we propose a short redline bundle to close the defend-vs-reimburse scoping and notice timing.

Hi Maria — Ben from Ops here. Quick technical summary and what will speed us up:

What we can provide (typical):
- Inference request logs: request_id, timestamp, model_version, truncated input_hash, output_hash, token_usage.
- Model artifact identifier: model_name + build_hash + quantization profile.
- KV/Cache snapshots: limited to session-level identifiers; we do not keep full KV history beyond retention window.
- Config metadata and deployment topology (region, node ids) to help correlate traces.

What we cannot provide: raw customer training datasets, or PII fields extracted from inputs unless you provide redacted/consented copies.

Delivery options:
- Small bundles: zipped sample files via secure link (we can host).
- Large bundles: presigned S3 upload; we will provide credentials for a 7-day window.

Triage tips to help us: include a seed request_id or a short list of sample timestamps, indicate whether you need anonymized logs vs. full traces, and flag any time ranges where model drift or altered behavior was observed.

I attached a simple evidence_schema.json that maps the field names we'll deliver. If you can populate a short checklist against that schema, we'll turn around the triage packet within 48 hours.

-Ben

Maria — following Ben's note, I've drafted targeted redlines to the Order Form and MSA to operationalize the intake and to narrow scope on AI-model-output claims. Key points (excerpt):

- Notice window: Customer must notify Redwood within 30 days of becoming aware of an alleged claim; Redwood will acknowledge receipt and provide a triage packet within 48 hours.
- Evidence scope: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide inference logs and model artifact identifiers necessary for claim assessment; Redwood will not be obligated to disclose raw customer training data.
- Defense control: For third-party IP claims arising solely from model outputs, the parties will cooperate; Redwood may elect to lead defense where the claim implicates model generation path. Any material costs advanced by Redwood will be subject to insurance offsets and indemnity caps as set forth in the order form.
- Confidential uploads: Evidence uploads will be via secure presigned S3 with limited retention; privileged communications will be preserved where applicable.

I also included a short operational SLA paragraph for evidence turnaround (48-hour triage + 5 business day delivery target for standard artifacts; exceptions documented).

If this aligns, Hannah can propose these as a package and we can ask BrightLabs for a one-paragraph acceptance or propose small edits. I included a DocuSign link placeholder for a narrow amendment to the order form.

Kimberly Park
